stories.title: Update: Delhi Traffic Police cite structural bottleneck at Barapullah merge point; Phase III traffic diverted towards NH-24/DND
stories.body: Delhi Traffic Police has attributed the congestion after the Barapullah Phase III opening to a structural bottleneck, ANI reported on Monday 5 October. It says about 8-9 lanes of traffic merge into 3 lanes at one point on the older flyover stretch, where the old Barapullah flyover, the new Phase III, the Sarai Kale Khan loop and the DND loop meet, each with three lanes. Personnel are posted at both merging points, and traffic from Phase III is being diverted towards NH-24/DND to ease the junction, the report says. It adds that navigation apps, including Google Maps, kept showing the route as clear despite the congestion.
stories.check: NEEDS CHECK: ANI gives 8-9 lanes merging into 3, while an earlier report (Asian News Channel, 1 Oct) said six lanes into three. The ANI report does not say which exits the NH-24/DND diversion covers or for how long; confirm with Delhi Traffic Police.

stories.title: Jamia professor receives Careers360 Faculty Research Award for most outstanding researcher in biochemistry and molecular biology
stories.body: Prof. Md. Imtaiyaz Hassan of Jamia Millia Islamia has received the Careers360 3rd Faculty Research Award for Most Outstanding Researcher in Biochemistry, Genetics and Molecular Biology, according to a Jamia press release dated Monday 5 October. The award, which carries a Rs 50,000 cash prize, was presented on Thursday 1 October at The Imperial, Janpath, New Delhi. The release says he works at the university's Center for Interdisciplinary Research in Basic Sciences and that the evaluation looked at Scopus-indexed output, citations and h-index. It quotes him thanking Careers360 and his students, research scholars, collaborators and colleagues.

stories.title: Jamia Senior Secondary School joins IIT Madras School Connect Programme
stories.body: Jamia Senior Secondary School has partnered with the IIT Madras School Connect Programme, according to a Jamia press release dated Monday 5 October. The programme offers eight-week online certificate courses for students in Classes IX to XII, in areas including data science and artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, economics and finance, law, digital humanities, ecology and forensic sciences. Students receive e-certificates from IIT Madras CODE on completing a course. The release names a computer science teacher as the school's contact for the initiative and says the principal facilitated the partnership with support from the university's leadership.
stories.check: The release page header shows the year 2025 and the PDF file names carry 2025, but the listing and the PDF text say 5 October 2026. Confirm the date with Jamia before publishing.
